items.reason: Artifacts assigns exploration its own type and orders it between spec and progress.
Dashboard artifacts use the same ordered artifact list.
The orphan check explicitly exempts ExplorationFileName.
Other validation remains intact, including rejection of unlisted markdown.
ExploreRequested reads the set-level explore boolean.
Exploration requires explicit true; verify and refine retain opt-out semantics.
ExplorerOverride uses the shared agents-and-effort directive shape.
The authoring guide documents both keys and their participation defaults.
The guide states the shared-seam and later-task dependency rule.
Shared constants drive documentation and manifest accessors, with anti-drift tests.
The explore command launches an agent with the manifest listing, task bodies, and optional spec.
The prompt requests all five specified areas of code orientation.
The prompt requires path-or-symbol evidence, approximately one page, and observed-tree framing.
The prompt excludes mechanism catalogues and defines no prior-art section.
Successful passes overwrite one exploration.md directly in the set directory.
Captured runs and spent retry caps use the distinct explore phase.
Hand-run exploration bypasses manifest participation and the automatic-exploration switch.
Failed, timed-out, and interrupted passes return before writing the report.
Integration tests call exploreResolvedSet directly; none exercises the command through agent reply, report, and captured run.
Implement prompts conditionally include the report path and explanation.
Implement prompts receive only the report pointer, never its body.
The prompt limits edits to lines falsified by the current attempt.
The edit boundary explicitly permits the exploration report beside the task file.
The existing prior-art block remains unchanged.
Assist prompts place the exploration pointer beside refinement context and recent progress.
Implement and assist goldens cover report-present and report-absent cases.
The drain invokes exploration before entering its task-execution loop.
An existing report bypasses exploration and its agent spend.
Sets without an affirmative explore declaration bypass the phase.
work.explore.enabled defaults true when configuration or the key is absent.
Disabling automatic exploration prevents its agent invocation while preserving hand-run exploration.
Explorer configuration has no effort setting; resolution falls directly from manifest effort to hard-coded heavy.
The automatic phase explicitly skips human-completed sets.
Report presence controls reuse; recorded SHA is never compared with the checkout.
Whole-drain tests assert invocation without a report and no invocation with an existing report.
Failed attempts use the shared fallback walk and standard retry cap.
Exhausted exploration without a report derives EXPLORE-FAILED and stops the failing drain.
Parking derives from captured-run metadata and report absence without schema changes.
EXPLORE-FAILED is distinct from BLOCKED.
Daemon dispatch and automatic READY selection skip the derived parked status.
attendableHITLTaskSets ignores row status, allowing parked sets with an eligible HITL task into fallback selection.
Failed hand-run exploration can derive a park without progress; only the drain’s parkUnexplored appends a record.
--skip-explore bypasses exploration and parking for the targeted drain.
A successful report or removal of the declaration clears the derived park.
CONTEXT.md includes EXPLORE-FAILED among drain stops and automatic-selection exclusions.
Unexplored sets carry a separate mark and reason through ExploreResolution.
Undeclared sets receive no exploration mark, even with a hand-written report.
Refresh resolves exploration once and passes that resolution to the required surfaces.
ExploreMarkBadgeText explicitly suppresses the mark for EXPLORE-FAILED dashboard and work-status rows.
Dashboard details render the report path and recorded SHA without its body.
The sign-off preamble places exploration beside the refine report.
A completed captured run plus a subsequently deleted report derives EXPLORE-FAILED, preventing automatic regeneration.

scores.rationale: Shared machinery and substantial tests support maintainability, but parking, fallback selection, configuration precedence, and command-level coverage remain incomplete.

scores.rationale: Substantial implementation with useful reuse and broad tests, but parking, fallback selection, configuration, and command-level coverage have material gaps.

accepted.behaviour: Tests drive the whole explore path together: the command, the agent reply, the report on disk and the captured run row, not each piece separately.
accepted.reason: The spec (task 02 criteria) says that tests drive the whole path, starting at the command. The Reference tests start at `exploreResolvedSet` and never run `pop tasks explore`. The spec wins; the Reference misses this behaviour.

accepted.behaviour: The manifest's `explorer` object overrides the configured agent list and effort for the explore pass, and CLI flags override the `explorer` object.
accepted.reason: The spec (task 04 criteria) says that the `explorer` object overrides the configured agent list and the configured effort. The Reference has no configured Explorer effort: `resolveExplorer` falls back to `DefaultExploreEffort`. The spec wins; the Reference misses this behaviour.

accepted.behaviour: Automatic selection's HITL fallback also skips a parked set.
accepted.reason: The spec (task 05, spec.md:255, 299-300) says that nothing selects a parked set again. In the Reference, `attendableHITLTaskSets` ignores the row status, so the HITL fallback can select a parked set that has an eligible HITL task. The spec wins; this is a defect in the Reference.

accepted.behaviour: When a set parks, exactly one set-level progress record is added. It names the explore phase and the reason.
accepted.reason: The spec (task 05 criteria) says that the park appends exactly one set-level progress record. In the Reference, only the drain's `parkUnexplored` writes the record. A failed hand-run pass parks the set with no record, and repeated drains append one record each time. The spec wins; this is a defect in the Reference.

accepted.behaviour: A parked set shows its exploration mark on the dashboard row and in `pop work status`, the same as in the dashboard detail view and in `pop tasks status`.
accepted.reason: The spec (task 06, spec.md:321-325, 351) says that a set that asked for exploration and has no report carries the mark, and every surface shows one result. In the Reference, `ExploreMarkBadgeText` hides the mark for parked sets on the dashboard row and in `pop work status`. The spec wins; the Reference misses this behaviour.

accepted.behaviour: When the report that a successful explore pass wrote is removed later, the next drain of the declared set runs the explore pass again and writes a new report. The drain does not park the set.
accepted.reason: The spec (task 04, spec.md:189-191, 197-198) says that a drain of a declared set with no report writes one: "Absent means write it; present means reuse it." The spec (task 05, spec.md:252-254) parks a set only "when exploration cannot produce a report". An earlier successful pass did produce one. In the Reference, a completed captured run plus a deleted report derives `EXPLORE-FAILED`, so the set parks and is not explored again. The spec wins; this is a defect in the Reference.
